originality.rationale: Comparison of the current-score auction from arXiv:2609.21974 with its exact lossless MILP scheduling objective; the inspected source explicitly leaves theoretical suboptimality open. Its authors' two single-agent predecessors do not define the competing multi-agent auction. Dedicated published-finding corpus searches, web searches and own ledger claim checks found no equivalent or dominating small-horizon counterexample. Remaining bibliographic risk is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Generic greedy scheduling or multi-agent control literature not returned by available semantic search could cover the general phenomenon; no claim of global uniqueness.
The full LQG cost includes an additive constant; the divergent ratio provably concerns only the nonnegative schedule-dependent objective, which is exactly the MILP minimized in the motivating source.
The counterexample uses degenerate process-noise covariance zero, allowed by finite-moment hypotheses but outside nondegenerate Gaussian simulation regimes.

value.rationale: Provides the missing negative worst-case multiplicative performance guarantee for the concrete current-benefit LQG scheduler proposed in arXiv:2609.21974. Structural reason is that an early slot can be wasted on a flexible agent while an expiring benefit is lost; stable two-agent two-stage Riccati-realizable weights make this a meaningful and small explicit boundary, not a generic invented scheduling example. Importantly only the schedule-dependent objective is compared.
